page.layout: One page of verse in italic, one column; a catchword at the lower right. No margin notes, no page number, no running head.

main_text.p: Immittit, torpent inuitae adiussa phalanges, Et magni piget incepti, tedetque laborum, Omnibus ante oculos leti presentis imago Terribilis iam iam de coelo afflarier igne Quisque sibi, pelagoue tegi surgente videtur; Horror ineft animis, trepidos pauor alligat artus; At in promissas fruftra, sol craftinus oras Detegat, antiquas repetant facto agmine sedes, Quin socios, ipsumque Ducem si forte repugnet Inuadant armis. Et iam delapsa polo nox Merserat humanas letheo flumine curas Solus adhuc, nec somnum oculis, nec corde Columbus Accipit; at partes animum deducit in omnes; Senserat ille famem totacrudescere classe, Et vulgi variare animos, certumque minari Exitium, spes nulla super, diuisa recessit Terra procul, passimque lues increscit eundo.
Continuo supplex oculos ad sydera tollit, Taliaque illacrimans duplicato poplite fatur,

Summe Pater, si non praedandi insana libido Aut amor imperij, patrijs me excedere tectis Suasit, & infido vitam committere vento, Sed tua diuersae colerent vt numina gentes, Pelle famem, vulgique nouos compesce tumultus. Si tamen has poenas mea facta indigna reposcunt, Ah nimium malefacta, grauique obnoxia poenae, Meme adige in tenebras, intorto fulmine solum

page.notes: The last word "Deiice" stands at the lower right as a catchword. Some letters in the italic verse are uncertain (e.g. "Inuadant", "Terribilis iam iam", "Meme"); the transcription follows the scan closely. The first line may be the page's opening; no cont marker is needed.
